story: Bristol Bay salmon escapement counting moves from hand clickers on ADF&G towers toward machines, through two federally funded BBRSDA pilots (UAV video plus AI on the Wood River, and automated sonar on the Naknek)

source_fetch_summary.notes: Fact-checker fetched NFWF press release, National Fisherman, Alaska Public Media/KDLG, Alaska's News Source, one ADF&G 404, the ADF&G Bristol Bay page, the ADF&G 2026 season summary PDF, bbrsda.com/news (empty) and fnsb.gov CivicAlerts. The NFWF slate PDF text was extracted once by the showrunner with scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py into out/2026-11-17/nfwf_emr_2026_slate.txt.

claims.claim: NOAA and NFWF awarded thirteen new Electronic Monitoring and Reporting grants in the 2026 slate.
claims.verbatim: Thirteen new grants totaling $3.4 million were awarded.

claims.claim: The 2026 EMR grants totaled $3.4 million.
claims.verbatim: Thirteen new grants totaling $3.4 million were awarded.

claims.claim: The 2026 EMR awards leveraged $4.2 million in matching contributions from grantees.
claims.verbatim: The awards leveraged $4.2 million in matching contribution from grantees

claims.claim: The 2026 EMR slate has a total conservation impact of $7.6 million.
claims.verbatim: providing a total conservation impact of $7.6 million

claims.claim: The 2026 EMR slate lists a $188,300 grant to the Bristol Bay Regional Seafood Development Association.
claims.notes: National Fisherman (C16) reports an NFWF EMR award to BBRSDA of $188,268 with a different description. Do NOT state they are the same award or that the scope changed.

claims.claim: The BBRSDA drone project lists $188,300 in matching funds.
The BBRSDA drone project's total amount is $376,600.
The NFWF project is titled Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles with AI Video Processing to Improve Salmon Counts in Bristol Bay.
claims.value: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles with AI Video Processing
claims.verbatim: Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles with AI Video Processing to Improve Salmon Counts in Bristol Bay (AK)

claims.claim: The NFWF-funded pilot uses drone video and AI video processing to improve sockeye escapement counts in the Wood River system.
claims.verbatim: Pilot the use of unmanned aerial vehicle video recording and AI video processing to improve sockeye salmon escapement counts in the Wood River system, Bristol Bay, Alaska.
claims.notes: A pilot, not an operational replacement for the towers.

claims.claim: The drone project will compare its results against traditional methods such as visual tower counts.
claims.verbatim: Project will compare results against traditional methods, like visual tower counts

claims.claim: The 2026 EMR slate also funds the Alaska Department of Fish and Game with $294,900 for a charter electronic logbook app.
claims.verbatim: Grantee: Alaska Department of Fish and Game Grant Amount: .....................................$294,900

claims.claim: The 2026 EMR slate funds the Alaska Sustainable Fisheries Trust with $293,600 for electronic logbooks in the Southeast Alaska troll fishery.
claims.verbatim: Grantee: Alaska Sustainable Fisheries Trust Grant Amount: .....................................$293,600
claims.notes: Match $300,000, total $593,600, 20 vessels. Alaska has three entries on the slate.

claims.claim: NFWF announced the $3.4 million in EMR grants on April 9th.
claims.verbatim: NFWF Announces $3.4 Million in Grants to Modernize Data Collection in U.S. Fisheries

claims.claim: The EMR grant program is a partnership between NFWF and NOAA Fisheries.
claims.verbatim: a partnership between NFWF and NOAA Fisheries

claims.claim: BBRSDA announced a second grant award from NFWF on October 29th, according to National Fisherman.
claims.verbatim: On Oct. 29, BBRSDA announced a second grant award of $188,268

claims.claim: National Fisherman reports BBRSDA's NFWF Electronic Monitoring and Reporting grant as $188,268.
claims.verbatim: a second grant award of $188,268 from the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation
claims.notes: The NFWF slate lists $188,300 for BBRSDA with a different description. Do not claim same award or scope change.

claims.claim: The Naknek project will deploy a hydroacoustic sonar system on the Naknek River near King Salmon, according to National Fisherman.
claims.verbatim: The project will deploy a hydroacoustic sonar system on the Naknek River near King Salmon, Alaska

claims.claim: The sonar system is meant to count returning salmon automatically.
claims.verbatim: to automatically count returning salmon

claims.claim: The sonar system will feed counts directly into an online dashboard.
claims.verbatim: feed the information directly into an online dashboard

claims.claim: The Naknek River will be the sonar system's first deployment site.
claims.verbatim: The Naknek River will serve as the first deployment site

claims.claim: SeaSignal Technologies, working with Coastal Measures and BioSonics, was selected through a competitive process to develop and operate the sonar system.
claims.verbatim: SeaSignal Technologies, working with Coastal Measures and BioSonics

claims.claim: The NFWF sonar grant period runs from June 1st, 2026 through May 31st, 2028.
claims.verbatim: The grant period runs from June 1, 2026, through May 31, 2028.

claims.claim: BBRSDA also received $499,400 through NOAA Fisheries' Saltonstall-Kennedy grant program.
claims.verbatim: $499,400 through NOAA Fisheries' Saltonstall-Kennedy (S-K) grant program

claims.claim: The Saltonstall-Kennedy project aims to increase demand for wild Alaska sockeye across the U.S. food service industry.
claims.verbatim: aims to increase demand for wild Alaska sockeye salmon across the U.S. food service industry

claims.claim: The two BBRSDA grants together total $687,668 in federal investment, according to National Fisherman.
claims.verbatim: Together, the two grants represent $687,668 in federal investment.

claims.claim: BBRSDA executive director Lilani Dunn said better information during the season means better decisions for everyone who depends on the fishery.
claims.verbatim: Better information during the season means better decisions for everyone who depends on this fishery

claims.claim: Dunn said sonar lets BBRSDA count fish across a wide stretch of the Naknek.
claims.verbatim: Sonar lets us count fish across a wide stretch of the Naknek

claims.claim: ADF&G has used counting towers in Bristol Bay for over 70 years.
claims.verbatim: For over 70 years, the Alaska Department of Fish and Game has used counting towers in Bristol Bay

claims.claim: The department has tracked Bristol Bay salmon escapement with towers since 1955.
claims.verbatim: This is how the department has been tracking salmon escapement since 1955

claims.claim: Most Bristol Bay escapement counts come from nine Fish and Game counting tower sites.
claims.verbatim: Most escapement counts across the Bay currently come from nine Fish & Game counting tower sites.

claims.claim: Fish and Game tower crews rotate through continuous shifts over 24 hours.
claims.verbatim: Fish & Game tower crews rotate through continuous shifts over 24-hours,

claims.claim: Tower crews count each passing salmon with a hand clicker in 10 minute intervals.
claims.verbatim: counting each salmon that swims by with a hand-clicker in 10 minute intervals.

claims.claim: Fish and Game was not directly involved in the drone project as of July.
claims.verbatim: At this stage, Fish & Game isn't directly involved in the project.

claims.claim: The project's drones fly just downstream of the Wood River towers.
claims.verbatim: Van Vactor's drones are just downstream of the Wood River towers

claims.claim: Project lead Norm Van Vactor said of the technology that it is the future.
claims.verbatim: I really think it's our future. I really do,

claims.claim: Team member Ian Chiu said the project will have a computer vision model trained to pick out salmon.
claims.verbatim: we'll have a computer vision model that will be trained on picking out salmon,

claims.claim: The team will likely need several thousand drone images for the model to reliably identify a fish, KDLG reported.
claims.verbatim: they'll likely need several thousand drone images for the model to learn how to reliably identify a fish,

claims.claim: BBRSDA and the Bristol Bay Economic Development Corporation are named among the partners supporting the drone research.
claims.verbatim: It's one of the partners supporting this research, alongside Bristol Bay Regional Seafood Development Association

claims.claim: The crew planned to test its models against Fish and Game tower counting data in the project's next phase.
claims.verbatim: The crew will test their models against Fish & Game tower counting data in the project's next phase.

claims.claim: The 2026 inshore Bristol Bay sockeye run was 45.7 million fish.
claims.verbatim: The 2026 inshore Bristol Bay sockeye salmon run of 45.7 million fish (Table 1)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Commercial Fisheries

claims.claim: The 2026 inshore run was 8% below the 49.6 million average of the latest 20 years.
claims.verbatim: was 8% below the 49.6 million average run for the latest 20-year period (2006
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Commercial Fisheries

claims.claim: 2026 was the first year since 2014 that the Bristol Bay inshore run was under 50 million fish.
claims.verbatim: This is the first year since 2014 that the total inshore run was less than 50 million fish.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Commercial Fisheries

claims.claim: Baywide sockeye escapement totaled 15.6 million fish in 2026.
claims.verbatim: Baywide escapement totaled 15.6 million fish (Table 3).
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Commercial Fisheries

claims.claim: The Wood River sockeye escapement was 2,586,432 fish in 2026.
claims.verbatim: Escapement- Wood tower 2,586,432
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Commercial Fisheries

claims.claim: ADF&G lists the Wood River optimal escapement goal for 2026 as 700,000 to 2,800,000 sockeye.
claims.verbatim: Wood River OEG 700,000
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Commercial Fisheries

claims.claim: ADF&G says the Kvichak, Naknek, Alagnak, Egegik and Wood rivers were within their escapement goal ranges in 2026.
claims.verbatim: The Kvichak, Naknek, Alagnak, Egegik, and Wood rivers were within their escapement goal ranges
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Commercial Fisheries

claims.claim: The 2026 Bristol Bay commercial sockeye harvest was 30.1 million fish.
claims.verbatim: The commercial harvest of 30.1 million sockeye salmon was 7% below the 32.3 million preseason forecast
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Commercial Fisheries

claims.claim: The preliminary 2026 exvessel value of all Bristol Bay salmon was $264.0 million.
claims.verbatim: The 2026 Bristol Bay preliminary exvessel value of $264.0 million for all salmon species
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Commercial Fisheries

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission approved Mayor Grier Hopkins' proposed moratorium on permits for large-scale data centers.
claims.verbatim: approved Mayor Grier Hopkins' proposed moratorium on permits for large-scale data centers

claims.claim: The commission extended the mayor's proposed 12-month moratorium to 18 months.
claims.verbatim: extending the mayor's proposed 12-month timeframe to 18

claims.claim: The commission extended the administration's research and recommendation deadline from six months to 10.
claims.verbatim: from six months to 10

claims.claim: Hopkins said the assembly vote will likely take place on January 14th.
claims.verbatim: a vote will likely take place on Jan. 14

claims.claim: Hopkins said the borough is researching how to turn the gray area of a data center on Eielson Air Force Base black and white.
claims.verbatim: We're doing some research into that and trying to figure out how to turn that gray area black and white.
